ai.description: *Hemidactylus sankariensis* is a small gecko reaching 45 mm SVL. It is pale brown with dark dorsal spots and possesses 6–8 subdigital lamellae on the fourth toe and 10–12 precloacal pores in males.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus sankariensis* is best distinguished by its strongly keeled, trihedral dorsal tubercles that are arranged in 16–18 distinct longitudinal rows.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus sankariensis* typically inhabits rocky outcrops and dry deciduous forests in the Indian subcontinent, often found at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Sankari Brookiish Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging after sunset to actively hunt for small insects and invertebrates on vertical surfaces.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus sankariensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus sankariensis* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu, India, typically inhabiting rocky outcrops at elevations between 300 and 1,000 meters.
